critic_risk_flags: Despite semantic appeal of mapping directly to H, an explicit H compartment in SEIHR is likely weakly identifiable with only 31 training weeks and a single sharp season. Separating I→H from H outflow can over-flex peak width/height and confound timing, especially without additional observables.

SEIRS introduces waning immunity, which is typically hard to identify in short single-season data and can spuriously create extra flexibility in tails/secondary-wave behavior. Given high peakiness, SEIR already provides a parsimonious way to shape the peak without adding a poorly identified waning process.
